answer_1.quote: The potential effectiveness of counterspeech as a hate speech mitigation strategy has motivated an increasing interest in Natural Language Generation (NLG) research towards the automation of its production.

answer_2.quote: We perform an extensive automatic evaluation on the CS generated for all the collected HS (i.e., 1626 CS examples in total, see Appendix A.4 for their distribution). In particular, we employ the following automatic metrics:

answer_4.quote: We recruited 17 graduate-level volunteer annotators for one hour, where they were given a brief presentation introducing the task, annotation guidelines, and annotated examples (see Appendix A.3 for more details).
answer_4.guideline: We rely on the following four dimensions defined on a 1-5 Likert scale: Cogency (COG) measures the amount and logical correctness of the supporting arguments provided by the CS: we use an adapted version of this metric from . Suitableness (SUI) measures how much a CS has a suitable style, meaning that it is polite, not hateful, it attacks the message and not the hater . Moreover, the CS should defend the minority attacked by the HS. Relevance (REL) measures how relevant the CS is to the content of the corresponding HS in terms of topic and target of hate . Informativeness (INF) measures how informative the CS is as a response to its HS in terms of the quantity and factual correctness of included facts .
